title: Service lifetimes and middleware order
summary: Register the DbContext and service in the request scope and order the middleware safely.

scenario.briefing: The product service is registered as a singleton while the DbContext is scoped, so the first request captures a context that later requests keep using. Register the service in the request scope and order the middleware so the exception handler wraps the pipeline.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Read the lifetimes: AddDbContext registers the context as scoped by default.
A singleton is created once and keeps its dependencies for the life of the application.
Register the product service with AddScoped so it matches the DbContext lifetime.
Place UseExceptionHandler before the other middleware so it wraps the pipeline.

misconceptions.description: Registering a scoped service as a singleton.
misconceptions.feedback: The singleton outlives the request and captures the first scoped DbContext. Match the lifetimes.

misconceptions.description: Assuming middleware registration order does not matter.
misconceptions.feedback: Middleware runs in registration order. A component only sees requests that reach it.

misconceptions.description: Resolving services from app.Services inside a handler.
misconceptions.feedback: That hides dependencies and bypasses scope validation. Inject through the constructor instead.

sections.title: Service lifetimes
sections.body: AddSingleton creates one instance for the application, AddScoped creates one per request, and AddTransient creates one per resolution. A singleton that depends on a scoped service captures that instance, which is a captive dependency and keeps the first request's state alive.

sections.title: Register the data layer
sections.body: AddDbContext registers the context as scoped. The options callback reads the connection string from configuration, so the value is not hardcoded in the pipeline.

sections.title: Constructor injection supplies the graph
sections.body: The controller already receives IProductService through its constructor. The container resolves that constructor from the registered lifetime, so the registration and the constructor must agree about scope.

sections.title: Middleware runs in order
sections.body: Each middleware component wraps the rest of the pipeline. UseExceptionHandler must be registered before the components whose exceptions it should catch. Authorization runs before endpoint execution, and MapControllers adds the controller endpoints.

artifact.title: Program.cs
artifact.caption: The product service is a singleton over a scoped DbContext, and the exception handler is registered after authorization.

findings.label: The singleton ProductService captures the scoped CatalogDbContext.
UseExceptionHandler is registered after UseAuthorization, so it cannot wrap authorization failures.
A singleton can depend on a scoped service because it resolves a fresh instance per request.
Middleware registration order has no effect on which requests reach the exception handler.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the lifetime and pipeline order are fixed.
The code only needs formatting changes.
Ship it; the registrations are safe.

steps.explanation: The singleton is created once, so it keeps the first request's scoped DbContext and every later request reuses it. The exception handler also sits after authorization, so authorization failures cannot be handled by it. Register the service as scoped and move the exception handler to the top of the pipeline.
